findings.evidence: Dyadic.lean:69-74 states conjugates of `hF.padicPow _ u`; Basic.lean:211-213 defines peripheral as "carries every element … to a conjugate of the `p`-adic power `y ^ u`".
findings.fix: Say "preserving the three peripheral conjugacy classes up to the common exponent `u`" (or "carrying each peripheral element to a conjugate of its `u`-th power"), matching the wording already used in Peripheral/Basic.lean:21-24.
findings.issue: "every dyadic unit exponent is realized by a continuous automorphism preserving the three peripheral conjugacy classes" overclaims: `exists_peripheralPowerAutomorphism_two` only gives φ(P) = cP⁻¹ * P^u * cP etc., so φ carries the class of P to the class of P^u, not to the class of P. For u ≠ 1 no peripheral class is preserved (even setwise): in the abelianization the exponent-sum vectors scale by u, which is exactly the argument of `IsPeripheralAut.exponent_unique` (Automorphism/Basic.lean:254-276).

findings.evidence: Dyadic.lean:24-29 has only `## Main results`; `grep -c "Main definitions"` matches 55 other files under TauCeti/Topology/Algebra/Group/Profinite, including Peripheral/Basic.lean and Peripheral/Lifting.lean.
findings.fix: Add a `## Main definitions` section listing `TauCeti.Peripheral.periphP`, `periphT`, `periphC` (with `periphC = cusp (basis e)`), as Peripheral/Basic.lean:30-39 does for `basis`, `cusp`, `peripheralTuple`.
findings.issue: The module docstring speaks only of `P`, `T`, `C` and never names the three public definitions `periphP`, `periphT`, `periphC`; there is no `## Main definitions` section, so a reader of the generated docs cannot connect the prose notation to the API, and the file's main definitional content is undocumented at module level.

summary: The module docstring claims the automorphism preserves the three peripheral conjugacy classes, which is false for any exponent other than 1 and is not what the theorem states, and the file's three public definitions are never named in the module docstring (no `## Main definitions`, unlike the sibling peripheral files).
